1 BASICS

Overview — What Is Shares?

Shares is a private, just-for-fun sports contest — one of Splash's "Other" contest formats, grouped alongside NFL Tiers, NFL Squares, NFL Wins Pool, and NFL 33. Unlike Survivor (one pick a week, elimination) or Pick'em (picking winners against the spread each week), Shares is a bankroll-based wagering contest.

Everyone starts with the same amount of pretend currency, called units, and uses it to make picks on real games — which team will win, by how much, how many points get scored, and so on. A correct pick adds units to your pile (your bank); a wrong one takes some away. When the season or schedule is over, whoever has the most units wins.

A few things set Shares apart from a typical pick'em or survivor contest:

  • You pick as much or as little as you want. There's no set number of picks each week, and no requirement to pick every game.
  • Nobody gets knocked out. A bad week doesn't eliminate you — you just have fewer units, and you can keep playing and climbing all season.
  • Each pick stands on its own. Every pick settles by itself when its game finishes, adding to or subtracting from your running total.
Think of it like: a season-long game where you're managing a pile of chips and trying to grow it bigger than everyone else's — not a weekly quiz with one right answer.
It's not real money. Units are pretend — they can't be bought, cashed out, or turned into money, and there's no cash prize. Every Shares contest is private and entertainment-only. (There is a separate, standard one-time service fee to run the overall Splash contest — the same as any other format — but that fee has nothing to do with the in-contest units themselves, which never represent real money regardless of standings. Pricing for Shares specifically is still TBD.)

2 BASICS

The Words You'll Hear

Shares borrows the vocabulary of a sportsbook, because its pick types are modeled on one. None of these terms involve real money — they're just the names for different kinds of picks and how they're scored.

The basics

  • Units — the pretend currency everyone plays with. Displayed as a plain number (e.g., "1,000 units").
  • Bank — a member's current pile of units, their running score. Goes up on wins, down on losses. Biggest bank at the end wins the contest.
  • Starting bank — the amount every member begins with, set by the commissioner and the same for everyone.
  • Market — a type of pick available on a game (e.g., "who wins" or "total points"). Each game offers several markets.
  • Odds — how much a pick pays if it wins, relative to what you put in. Odds lock in the moment you make the pick.
  • Vig (also "juice") — a small built-in cut taken out of winning picks, similar to how a sportsbook keeps the odds in balance. Set by the commissioner as a percentage; only affects winnings on picks made after a change.
  • Lock — the moment a game closes for picking. Football locks at kickoff; baseball locks at first pitch.
Reading American odds: a minus number (e.g., −110) is a favorite — it's how many units you'd risk to win 100. A plus number (e.g., +150) is an underdog — it's how many units you'd win on a 100-unit pick. A bigger plus number means a bigger underdog and a bigger payout.

3 SETUP

Setting Up a Shares Contest

Creating a Shares contest follows the same overall contest-creation flow as every other Splash format — it's the format-selection step where Shares differs.

Step 1: Choose a contest format

On the "Choose a contest format" screen, select the Other tab (next to Survivor and Pick'em). This reveals the full list of other available formats: NFL Tiers, NFL Squares, NFL Wins Pool, NFL 33 – Closest Score, and NFL Shares.

Select NFL Shares, then click Continue.

Step 2: Name your contest

The final step is the same naming screen used across every format: an optional Custom Contest Name field (up to 256 characters), a Back button, and the Create contest button.

Service fee reminder: a one-time service fee applies when the contest starts (this is the standard Splash contest-hosting fee, separate from the pretend in-contest units — exact pricing for Shares is still TBD). Commissioners can waive it later by setting up Contest Vault (powered by LeagueSafe).
Wording: Splash Shares contests are always invite-only — never "free-to-play."

4 BASICS

What You Can Pick, By League

Shares currently supports three leagues, and each offers a different set of pick types. A single contest can run one league, or a compatible combination.

LeaguePick types availableGames lock atSchedule
NFL (pro football)Money line, spread, parlay, teaserKickoffWeekly
College football (NCAAF)Money line, spread, parlayKickoffWeekly
MLB (baseball)Money line, run line, total, parlayFirst pitchDaily

Two rules worth knowing, because they come up constantly:

  • Teasers are NFL only. They aren't offered for college football or baseball.
  • Football and baseball can't be mixed in one contest. Football runs on a weekly schedule and baseball on a daily one, so a contest is either a football contest (NFL, college, or both combined) or a baseball contest — never a blend of the two.
Why "weekly" vs "daily" matters: in a football contest, picks are organized by week. In a baseball contest, they're organized by day. Same idea — a batch of games you can pick from — just on the natural rhythm of each sport.

5 MEMBER VIEW

My Entries — The Home Dashboard

Once a member enters a Shares contest, the Home tab is their landing page, built around three cards:

  • Balance — shows Available units (ready to wager) separately from At risk units (currently tied up in pending picks)
  • My positions — every pick submitted from the board lands here; shows "No positions yet" until the first pick is placed
  • Recent updates — an activity feed (e.g., a new member joining the contest, with a date stamp)
Tip: "Available" vs. "At risk" is the fastest way to see how much of your bank is free to wager versus already committed to pending picks.

Entries

Your entry is your seat in the contest — it holds your bank and your picks. Depending on how the commissioner set things up, a member may be able to have more than one entry in the same contest (think of it as playing multiple hands). Each entry has its own separate bank and its own picks; the "My Entries" area lets a member see all of them and switch between them. Any pick made always applies to whichever entry is currently active.

The left-hand navigation — visible on every page — includes Home, Picks, Pending, Standings, History, Contest details for all members, plus a Commissioner section (Dashboard, Contest settings, Entrants manager, Invites manager) visible only to the commissioner.

6 MEMBER VIEW

The Picks Board — Placing Singles

The Picks tab is the heart of a Shares contest. At the top sits a horizontally scrollable week selector — Preseason Week 2, Preseason Week 3, Week 1 through Week 8 and beyond — each showing its date range.

Below that, every scheduled game for the selected week appears as its own card, showing three odds columns: Spread, Total, and Money Line.

On the right, the Pick Slip panel starts empty ("Your slip is empty. Pick a game to start."). It's a running list of what you're about to submit, showing the units and potential payout before you commit. Clicking any odds box — a spread, total, or money line — highlights that selection and adds it to the Pick Slip as a single wager.

Note: the Pick Slip shows a Risk field (units wagered) and calculates the Return automatically based on the odds. A max stake (e.g., 100 units) is enforced per pick.

7 MEMBER VIEW

Parlays & Teasers, With Real Numbers

Next to the Picks tab sits a Parlays tab. Switching to it changes how the Pick Slip behaves: instead of one independent wager per selection, legs chosen from different games combine into a single parlay — every leg must hit for it to pay out. If even one leg misses, the whole parlay loses.

As legs are added, the Pick Slip calculates Risk, Return, Gross return, Vig deducted, and Remaining after picks.

Tip: the Pick Slip can also hold several independent singles at once (not parlayed together). A "Stake all singles (X)" bulk field applies the same stake to every single at once, while still showing each leg's individual Risk/Return.
All-or-nothing batch submit: when submitting multiple picks together, Splash processes them as one batch — either the whole batch submits, or none of it does.

Teasers (NFL only)

A teaser is a friendlier version of a parlay, available for NFL spreads and totals only. It lets you shift every line in your favor by a set number of points — making each leg easier to hit — in exchange for a smaller payout. Like a parlay, every leg still has to hit.

Worked examples (illustrative unit figures)

These numbers show the shape of the payout, not guaranteed figures — actual amounts depend on the odds at pick time and your contest's settings.

PlayStakeWhat happensApprox. payout
Single
(baseline)		100 units on one team's money line at −110One game, roughly even odds — the best chance of hitting~91 units profit if it hits
3-leg parlay100 units across three −110 picks, bundledAll three must win; miss any one and the whole parlay loses~696 units back (~596 profit) — roughly 6.5× the single's profit
2-leg, 6-point teaser100 units on two NFL favorites (e.g., −7.5 → −1.5, and −3.5 → +2.5)Both lines move 6 points in your favor, making each leg easier to hit~183 units back (~83 profit) — smaller than the parlay, but with a real cushion on the margin
You want…Reach for…
The biggest possible payout, and confidence in several picksA parlay — highest reward, lowest chance of hitting
A better chance of winning, with a cushion on close games (NFL)A teaser — safer legs, smaller payout
The simplest play with the best odds of landingA single — one game, one result
Push: if a pick ties the line exactly (e.g., you pick −7 and the team wins by exactly 7), nobody's right or wrong — that pick is simply refunded. In a parlay, that leg drops out and the rest carries on.

8 BASICS

How a Pick Plays Out, Start to Finish

  1. You make a pick. Choose a game, a market, and how many units to put on it. The odds are locked in at that moment.
  2. The game locks. At kickoff or first pitch, that game closes — no more picks or changes on it.
  3. The game finishes and your pick settles. Splash checks the result and decides your pick automatically. A win pays units into your bank based on the odds you locked in; a loss takes your staked units. A push is refunded.
  4. Your bank updates, and so do the standings. Every settled pick moves your running total, and the leaderboard re-sorts by bank.
Note: settlement is automatic and happens shortly after each game ends — there's a brief delay while results come in and get processed, so a bank may take a moment to reflect a just-finished game.

9 MEMBER VIEW

Pending, Standings & History

Pending

The Pending tab lists picks that have been placed but haven't locked or settled yet. Before any picks are made, it shows an empty state ("No pending picks") with a Make a pick shortcut button.

Commissioner view: when a commissioner opens their own Pending tab, a banner reads "COMMISSIONER VIEW — YOU SEE MORE THAN MEMBERS DO," flagging that commissioners have extra visibility members don't.

Standings

The Standings tab ranks every entry by bank. Filter pills let you view Season, This week, Last week, Last 7 days, or Custom, plus a search bar. Columns: #, Entry, Bank, Net, Record, Risk, Return.

Privacy by default: other players' picks are hidden until the game locks — by default you can't see what someone else picked on a game until that game has kicked off (or first pitch), so nobody can copy live picks. After lock, visibility depends on the contest's Pick visibility setting. Standings visibility can likewise be set to show the full leaderboard or a more limited view, depending on the contest.

History

The History tab charts a Bank Trajectory line graph over time and lists settled picks below.

12 CONTEST SETTINGS

Contest Settings — General

Commissioners reach every setting through Contest settings → Edit pool settings, organized into five tabs: General, Format & Wagering, Picks, Bank, Design.

  • Contest name — editable at any time
  • Description — free-text field shown to entrants
  • Late entry — Closed, or Open with starting bank (late joiners get the full starting bank, not a prorated amount)

The Danger zone holds a red Cancel contest button. Clicking it opens a confirmation modal requiring a typed reason plus a checked "I understand this can't be undone" box before the final Cancel button activates.

Warning: cancelling voids and refunds all open wagers back to each member's bank and closes the contest for good — there is no undo.

13 CONTEST SETTINGS

Contest Settings — Format & Wagering

This is where the wagering rules of the contest live.

  • League Type — NFL (NCAAF or combined on other versions of this contest)
  • Pick types — checkboxes: Money Line, Spread, Total, Teaser, Parlay
  • Max units per pick — caps how much can be risked on any single pick
  • Vig (%) — the commission built into payouts
  • Parlay minimum/maximum legs — how many legs a parlay must/can contain
  • Max leg spread (days) — how many days apart the games in one parlay can be
  • Spread odds — default juice applied to spread bets
  • Mixed-league parlays — allows a parlay to combine legs across leagues (relevant for combined NFL+NCAAF contests)
Note: disabling a pick type here removes it from the picks board entirely. Remember: teasers are NFL-only regardless of this setting — they won't appear for NCAAF or MLB contests. Changing Vig only affects picks made after the change; it never touches picks already settled.

15 CONTEST SETTINGS

Contest Settings — Bank

Controls the two numbers that define everyone's bankroll.

  • Share price (units) — the baseline unit value. Flagged "Never editable" — fixed for the life of the contest.
  • Starting bank (units) — how many units everyone begins with. Flagged "Locks at contest start."

What can be changed later — and what can't

WhenExamplesWhy
AnytimeMax units per pick, vig, which pick types are allowed, parlay/teaser limits, privacy settings, late-entry policyThese shape future picks and can be tuned as the contest runs; changes only affect picks made after the change
Locks once the contest startsWhich sports are enabled, the starting bankChanging these after people are playing would move the goalposts
Fixed for the whole contestShare priceSet once at creation and defines the contest; changing it later would rewrite the basis everyone joined under
Warning: double-check Share price and Starting bank before the contest goes live — neither can be corrected once entrants are underway.

17 COMMISSIONER

Commissioner Tools While the Contest Runs

Beyond initial setup, commissioners have several tools for managing a live contest:

ActionWhat it does
Adjust a member's bankAdd or remove units from a member's bank directly — for corrections, prizes, or house rules. Every adjustment is recorded in the contest's ledger and visible to members, and can be reversed but never silently deleted.
Manager pickPlace a pick on a member's behalf (if enabled). Follows all normal rules and is labeled in the feed as Commissioner-placed.
Void a pickCancel a pick and refund it. If it had already won, the payout is reversed first, then the stake refunded — netting back to exactly what was put in. Voiding a parlay voids all its legs together.
Adjust the schedule windowAdd future weeks/days to the contest, or remove ones that haven't started and have no picks on them. Weeks/days that already have picks can't be dropped.
Finalize or cancelEnd the contest. Cancelling refunds all open picks and closes every entry. Finalizing wraps up a contest whose games are done.
Bank adjustments are transparent by design: when a commissioner changes someone's bank, it isn't hidden — it shows in the contest's ledger for everyone, with direction and amount, and it can be reversed. This keeps the contest honest, with no quiet edits to anyone's score.

19 REFERENCE

FAQ

Q: A member wants to deposit money or cash out their winnings.

A: Units in a Shares contest are pretend currency and are never real money — there's nothing to deposit into the contest and nothing to cash out based on standings. (Separately, Splash may charge a standard one-time service fee to run the overall contest, the same as any other format — pricing for Shares is still TBD — but that fee is unrelated to the in-contest units or who's winning.)

Q: "My parlay lost even though most of my picks won."

A: Every leg in a parlay must hit for it to pay out. If even one leg misses, the whole parlay loses — that's the trade-off for its much bigger payout.

Q: "Why can't I see what other players picked?"

A: By default, other players' picks on a game are hidden until that game locks (kickoff or first pitch), so nobody can copy live picks. After lock, visibility depends on the contest's Pick visibility setting.

Q: "The Commissioner changed my unit total — can they do that?"

A: Yes. Commissioners can adjust a member's bank for corrections, prizes, or house rules. Every adjustment shows in the contest's ledger for everyone to see, and can be reversed but never silently deleted.

Q: "My pick disappeared / my units came back."

A: This is most likely a voided pick — the commissioner (or a game postponement/cancellation) can void a pick, which refunds it. If it had already won, the payout is reversed first, then the stake refunded, netting back to exactly what was put in.

Q: "A game finished but my bank hasn't updated."

A: Settlement is automatic but not instant — there's a brief delay while results come in and get processed. Give it a little time before assuming something's wrong.

Q: "Can I be knocked out of a SHARES contest?"

A: No. A bad week just means a smaller bank — you can keep playing and climbing the entire season. Nobody is eliminated.

Q: "Why can't I add a college football game to my teaser?"

A: Teasers are only available for NFL games. NCAAF and MLB don't offer the teaser pick type.

20 REFERENCE

Glossary

TermDefinition
UnitsThe pretend currency everyone plays with. Spent to make a pick, won when it hits.
BankA member's current pile of units — their running score.
AvailableUnits free to wager (not tied up in a pending pick).
At riskUnits currently committed to picks that haven't settled yet.
Starting bankThe amount of units every member begins with; set by the commissioner, locks at contest start.
Share priceThe contest's underlying unit-value baseline; fixed for the life of the contest.
MarketA type of pick available on a game (e.g., who wins, total points).
OddsHow much a pick pays if it wins, relative to the stake; locked in at pick time.
Vig / JuiceA small built-in cut taken out of winning picks, set by the commissioner as a percentage.
LockThe moment a game closes for picking (kickoff for football, first pitch for baseball).
Money lineA pick on who wins the game outright, regardless of margin.
Spread (football)A pick on the margin of victory; the favorite is handicapped, the underdog gets a head start.
Run line (MLB)Baseball's version of the spread, set at 1.5 runs.
Total (Over/Under)A pick on the combined score of both teams, not on who wins.
ParlayA single pick bundling several legs together for a bigger payout; every leg must hit.
Teaser (NFL only)A friendlier parlay for spreads/totals that shifts every line in your favor for a smaller payout.
LegOne individual pick inside a parlay or teaser.
PushA tie against the line; the pick (or that leg of a parlay) is simply refunded.
EntryA member's seat in the contest, holding one bank and its own picks. Some contests allow multiple entries per member.
Pick SlipThe running list of picks about to be submitted, showing units and potential payout.
Max leg spread (days)The maximum number of days apart the games in a single parlay's legs can be.
Mixed-league parlaysA setting allowing a parlay to combine legs from different leagues in a combined contest.
Late entryThe policy for whether/how new entrants can join after the contest has started.
Pool bankThe total combined units across every entry in the contest.
Contest VaultSplash's optional integration (via LeagueSafe) for collecting and distributing the contest's service fee online.
VoidA commissioner action that cancels a pick and refunds it, reversing any payout first if it had already won.
